t:
Section 216 of the Older Americans Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3020f) is amended—
    (1) in subsection (a), by striking “2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005” and inserting “2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011.”; and 
    (2) in subsections (b) and (c), by striking “year” and all that follows through “years”, and inserting “years 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011”.

fable.w: This section only amends the fiscal years listed in section 216 of the Older Americans Act, which is an authorization-of-appropriations provision. A tempting reading is that the Older Americans Act involves state agencies and advisory bodies, but nothing in this text requires consultation, comment, hearings, rulemaking, or any other involvement of parties outside the federal government. It is a technical extension of years with no outside-party process.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that updates fiscal years in a statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely changes dates.
qwen_block.s: Section 216 of the Older Americans Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3020f) is amended— (1) in subsection (a), by striking “2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005” and inserting “2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011.”; and (2) in subsections (b) and (c), by striking “year” and all that follows through “years”, and inserting “years 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011”.

opus.w: This amendment only changes the fiscal years in Section 216 of the Older Americans Act, from 2001–2005 to 2007–2011. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The fact that the Act as a whole involves outside groups doesn't put any participation process into this purely technical date change.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be to assume that because the Older Americans Act sets up programs that work with states and outside organizations, this amendment must involve participation. That reading fails because the amendment only replaces fiscal years in Section 216, which is the Act's authorization-of-appropriations provision. It says nothing about consulting anyone, holding hearings or comment periods, creating advisory bodies, or giving anyone a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely updates the fiscal years referenced in the Older Americans Act. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) regarding a federal decision. It is a technical amendment to statutory text, not a procedural requirement for participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 216 of the Older Americans Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3020f) is amended— (1) in subsection (a), by striking “2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005” and inserting “2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011.”; and (2) in subsections (b) and (c), by striking “year” and all that follows through “years”, and inserting “years 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Older Americans Act involves services for the public, any amendment to it implicitly involves public participation. However, this specific section only updates fiscal years and does not establish any new process for consulting with or involving outside parties in a decision.
